entry.title: Introducing stinger: a hived plugin for matching operations of interest

link.title: Introducing stinger: a hived plugin for matching operations of interest

entry.content:
![stinger-icon.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXFsp9c8oCSZU5jyzc8nfwtogRmnurPBZaSJD2PFUDJ2f/stinger-icon.png) I'd like to share **stinger**, a plugin for `hived` that watches every operation the node applies and hands the ones you care about to your own process, as JSON lines on a unix socket, as soon as the block is irreversible, or under a millisecond after it is applied if you ask for that. You describe what you care about in a small, readable JSON rules file. No database, no replay, no polling loop. ## What is stinger Stinger sits inside the node, on the writer thread, right where blocks are applied. For every operation, real or virtual, it checks the operation against your rules. When one matches, the operation is sent to a socket your program is reading from, together with the block number, timestamp and transaction id. Delivery runs on a separate sink thread, so a slow consumer never holds up hived. A rule looks like this: ```json { "name": "shop-paid", "match": "op_type in (transfer, fill_recurrent_transfer) and to = \"shop\"", "exec": { "type": "socket" } } ``` That's a complete rule. `name` is how the match will be labelled on the stream, `match` is a boolean expression, `exec` says where the match goes: to the socket, or just to the node's log. Your side of it is a few lines in whatever language you like: ```python import json, socket s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM) s.connect("/run/hived/stinger.sock") for line in s.makefile("r"): rec = json.loads(line) if rec["kind"] == "match": print(rec["rules"], rec["block"], rec["op"]) ``` The socket is created readable and writeable by its owner only, so run the consumer as the same user as hived. The first line on every connection is a greeting: ```json {"kind":"hello","seq":41,"version":1,"delivered":{"head":null,"irreversible":111339249}} ``` It exists because the socket keeps no history. `delivered` says where each stream stands, so you know what this connection will give you and what you have to fetch from the APIs: everything up to block 111339249 is yours to backfill, and everything after it will arrive on the socket. Irreversible matches at or below that block can still follow the greeting, because they were already on their way when you connected; your backfill has them, so skip them. `seq` is the position of the last record the node rendered, so a consumer that reconnects can tell from its new greeting how many records it missed while it was away. `version` is the format's; refuse one you don't know. Then the matches follow. This is what one line of the stream looks like (the operation is in the same form `block_api` and `account_history_api` return): ```json {"kind":"match","seq":42,"delivery":"irreversible","rules":["shop-paid"],"block":111339250,"timestamp":"2026-11-03T12:00:00","trx_id":"6e1a...","trx_in_block":3,"op_in_trx":0,"virtual_op":false,"op":{"type":"transfer_operation","value":{"from":"alice","to":"shop","amount":{"amount":"5000","precision":3,"nai":"@@000000021"},"memo":"order 1234"}}} ``` `rules` lists every rule that matched the operation, so one operation is one line however many rules hit it. `delivery` is the class the line was delivered in, irreversible or head. `block`, `timestamp`, `trx_id`, `trx_in_block` and `op_in_trx` place the operation exactly where account history would, and `virtual_op` tells a virtual operation apart from one that was in a transaction. `op` is the operation itself. A match too large to send in one line arrives with `"op": null` and an `op_omitted` field saying why; the coordinates are still there, so you can fetch the operation from the API. ## Why stinger Most of the things people commonly want from the chain are small. "Tell me when someone pays my account." "Give me every `custom_json` my app emits." "Tell me every time my witness produces a block." "Alert on transfers over some threshold." Today the choices for that are: - **Run HAF.** It's great if you need SQL over the full history, but it's a big thing to set up and keep running, and most of the time you only need one or two operation types going forward. - **Poll the APIs.** `get_ops_in_block`, `account_history`, or streaming blocks over HTTP and filtering on your side. It works, it's what [hive-index](https://index.hive-adventures.com/) does today, but you end up pulling the whole chain through your process to pick out a tiny fraction of it. You also pay latency for polling and put load on an API node for data you throw away. - **Patch hived.** Nobody does that, for good reasons. Stinger is the **missing small option**: the node already sees every operation, so let it do the filtering, and let your program receive just the matches. ## Design A few decisions shape it, and they're worth spelling out because they're also the limits. **Matching happens in the node, but it's not code.** Rules are boolean expressions over a fixed set of attributes, parsed once at startup and put into an index (a be-tree, a structure built for matching one event against many subscriptions at once). There's no script and no user code on the consensus path, so the cost is a microsecond or so per operation for typical rule sets. On a live node that comes to a fraction of a millisecond per block. A node asked to match while it syncs (off by default) syncs about 8% slower with a handful of rules; the numbers are in the performance section below. **Irreversible by default, head if you ask.** Hive normally makes a block irreversible within about a second of applying it, so by default a block's matches are delivered once they can't be undone. You never see a fork. A rule can opt into `"delivery": "head"` to skip that wait, and then the stream also carries `block_applied`, `switch_fork` and `irreversible` markers, so it can retract and settle on its own. **The node keeps nothing.** No history, no per-consumer state. The stream is live only. Every record is self-contained, the greeting on connect tells you where the stream stands, and anything older than that you fetch from the regular APIs. This is deliberate: stinger isn't trying to be HAF. **The writer never waits.** Matches go from the writer thread to a sink thread through a queue bounded in bytes. If a consumer stops reading, it gets disconnected. If the sink falls behind the writer, the oldest waiting blocks are dropped and every consumer receives a `dropped` record naming which blocks. It fails loudly and the node is unaffected. **No outbound network.** The sinks are a log line and a local socket. If you want webhooks, a message queue or WebSockets, write a small bridge on the far side of the socket. That's where retries, timeouts and TLS belong, not inside `hived`. It's meant for API and seed nodes. It's extra work on the block-apply path, so don't put it on a witness node. ## What a rule can test | Attribute | Meaning | |---|---| | `op_type` | operation type, by name (`transfer`, `custom_json`, `producer_reward`) or number; virtual ops included | | `is_virtual` | whether the op is virtual; used bare: `is_virtual`, `not is_virtual` | | `impacted_accounts` | every account the op touches, same as account history sees it | | `amount`, `symbol` | the op's own `amount` field in satoshis (so `1000000` is 1000.000 HIVE) and its symbol; only ops that actually have an `amount` field define it | | `custom_id` | the `id` of a `custom_json` | | `from`, `to` | the op's own `from` and `to` fields: transfers, savings, escrows, recurrent transfers | Expressions support `=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `in` / `not in` with a list, `"name" in impacted_accounts` for a single account and `one of` / `none of` / `all of` with a list for several, and `and` / `or` / `not` with parentheses. An undefined attribute fails every test, so `custom_id` only ever matches a `custom_json` and `amount` only an operation that has one. That is still ten operation types (transfers, power-ups, savings, converts, recurrent transfers and their virtual fills), so a rule on `amount` normally says which `op_type` it means. An `op_type` term is worth adding to any rule anyway: the index then only shows the rule operations of that type, which is what keeps large rule sets cheap (the numbers are in the performance section). A rule that doesn't parse stops the node at startup and tells you which rule. ## Example use cases - **Payment notifications.** A shop or a service waits for transfers to its account and fulfils the order from the memo. `to = "shop"` on `transfer` and `fill_recurrent_transfer`, and you're done. - **Dapp ingestion.** Subscribe to your own `custom_json` ids and feed them straight into your backend. No block streaming, no filtering on your side. This is the one I'm most interested in for hive-index. - **Witness monitoring.** Match `producer_reward` for your witness with head delivery and alert if it goes quiet for longer than a round (for a top witness; a backup witness isn't scheduled every round, so give it a longer window). - **Early large-transfer alerts.** `amount > 1000000` on HIVE transfers with head delivery, pushed to a bot. - **Account activity feed.** Everything that touches a given set of accounts, real ops only, for a dashboard or a notification service. - **Rewards tracking.** `author_reward` and `curation_reward` for a team of accounts, for payouts or accounting. - **NFT processing.** An NFT app that keeps its state in `custom_json` matches its own ids, plus the `account_created` virtual op so it knows which account names in the payloads are real. Everything it needs is in the match record, and its own state lives in its own database. ## Example config The rules file: ```json { "rules": [ { "name": "large-hive-transfer", "match": "op_type = transfer and symbol = \"HIVE\" and amount > 1000000", "exec": { "type": "socket" }, "delivery": "head" }, { "name": "alice-activity", "match": "\"alice\" in impacted_accounts and not is_virtual", "exec": { "type": "log" } }, { "name": "shop-paid", "match": "op_type in (transfer, fill_recurrent_transfer) and to = \"shop\"", "exec": { "type": "socket" } }, { "name": "splinterlands-market", "match": "op_type = custom_json and custom_id = \"sm_market\"", "exec": { "type": "log" } }, { "name": "team-rewards", "match": "op_type in (author_reward, curation_reward) and impacted_accounts one of (\"alice\", \"bob\", \"carol\")", "exec": { "type": "socket" } }, { "name": "my-witness-produced", "match": "op_type = producer_reward and \"mywitness\" in impacted_accounts", "exec": { "type": "socket" }, "delivery": "head" } ] } ``` And the `config.ini` side: ```ini plugin = stinger stinger-rules-file = rules.json stinger-socket = /run/hived/stinger.sock ``` Relative paths are taken from the data directory, like the other `hived` path options. Two more knobs exist, both optional: `stinger-ready-queue-mb` (memory for matches waiting to be delivered, 128 MB by default) and `stinger-match-during-sync` (also match blocks received while the node is still syncing; off by default, replayed blocks are never matched). ## Performance Keeping hived fast matters, so I measured what enabling the plugin costs, both in live sync and in replay. Replay isn't how you'd use it (replayed blocks are never matched; I patched that out for the measurement), but it's the cleanest measurement of the matcher itself. All runs are a Release mainnet `hived` on the first 5M blocks of the chain (about 19.8M operations, 4 per block on average), on an 8-core box, inside a container. The live-sync runs are a fresh node syncing over P2P from a seed node on the same machine, with `stinger-match-during-sync` turned on, which is the closest I can get to real conditions without a network in the way. With default settings a syncing node doesn't match at all, so the sync figures are the price of asking for the backfill, not something every node pays. Each stinger run is compared with a base run made right next to it. The base sync itself ranged from 702 to 728 s over the day, so read the live-sync percentages as good to a few points, not to the decimal. With a set of 6 rules much like the example above (two large transfer rules, a power-up threshold, two account watches, one `custom_id`; log sinks, 13 matches in 5M blocks): | scenario | base | stinger | overhead | |---|---|---|---| | live P2P sync to 5M | 702 s | 758 s | +56 s (+8.1%) | | replay to 5M, matching forced on | 173 s | 202 s | +29 s (+17%) | On replay that's about **6 µs per block**, or **1.5 µs per operation**, and that's the matcher: building an event for each operation and searching the index. Live sync costs about 11 µs per block. The matching part carries over one to one; the other 5 µs or so per block is bookkeeping that only runs for live blocks (fork tracking, the irreversible window) and doesn't depend on the number of rules. It's a bigger percentage on replay because replay is about 4x faster per block than sync (no signature checks, no P2P, no undo sessions). The writer thread is saturated during sync, so every microsecond spent matching lands directly on sync throughput; there's no hiding it. A live node is the opposite case: it applies one block every three seconds, and at 1.5 µs per operation even a 100-operation block is about 0.15 ms of matching. Memory doesn't move at all with log-only rules. Where does the per-operation cost go? Not into the be-tree search. It's building the event for each operation: collecting the impacted accounts, pulling out the typed fields, interning the strings. That's a fixed cost you pay once per operation regardless of how many rules there are, and it's the obvious thing to optimise next. Then there's how the cost scales with the number of rules, which depends on the shape of the rule: | rules | 50 | 200 | 1000 | |---|---|---|---| | `op_type = X and ...`, spread over op types | +17% | +17% | +19% | | `"account" in impacted_accounts`, no `op_type` | +27% | +55% | +186% | (Replay overhead over 5M blocks. The live-sync check on the 1000-rule files took 770 s and 1092 s against a 728 s base, +5.7% and +50%, consistent with the above. That +5.7% is below the 6-rule +8.1% only because its base run was slower: in absolute terms it's 770 s against 758 s.) Rules with an `op_type` term are effectively free in bulk: the index partitions on operation type, so an operation only reaches the rules for its own type, and 1000 of them cost about the same as 6. Rules that watch an account across all operation types can't be partitioned yet, so every operation is tested against every one of them, at about 15 ns per operation per rule. It's linear, and at a few dozen such rules it's fine, but a thousand of them make the node almost 3x slower on replay. Loading 1000 rules at startup takes about 10 ms either way. The last thing I checked was the delivery path under the worst case: one rule matching every operation, pushing all 19.8M records (10 GB of JSON) down the socket to a consumer writing them to disk. That costs +20% on sync, of which about +13% is just rendering the JSON, which happens whether or not anyone is connected. Peak RSS stayed within 10 MB of the base with the consumer attached. In the run with nobody connected it peaked about 240 MB higher, and I haven't tracked down why yet. The consumer was never disconnected and every block was delivered. The hardest moment is a hardfork block with 106k virtual operations (53 MB of matches in one block); the queue is bounded in bytes precisely so that a block like that doesn't push its neighbours out. ### Latency How long after a block is applied does a match reach your program? I measured it on a local testnet: two producing nodes holding the 21 witnesses, two API nodes running stinger (one matching a tenth of the transfers, one matching everything), a Python consumer on each socket, all on one box, with transfers at 10, 100 and 1000 ops per block. | matched ops per block | 1 | ~10 | ~100 | ~1000 | |---|---|---|---|---| | head delivery, block applied -> match at the consumer, p50 / p99 | 0.1 / 0.6 ms | 0.3 / 0.8 ms | 0.9 / 2.3 ms | 6 / 16 ms | Handing a block's matches to the sink thread takes about 50 µs; the rest is rendering the JSON, about 11 µs per record. The table times each match, so in a block where all 1000 operations match the median match arrives after 6 ms and the last one after 12 ms (21 ms p99). Irreversible delivery adds however long the chain takes to make the block irreversible, which is not stinger's cost: 3-5 ms on the local testnet, and on mainnet, polling public API nodes for 43 minutes, the last irreversible block was already equal to head in about 90% of samples and otherwise caught up within a second. A deliberately slow consumer (one line every 50 ms) was disconnected after about 14 s, once it had fallen 4 MB behind, with nothing dropped and a negligible effect on the other consumer on the socket (about 1 µs per record). None of this is optimised yet. The fixed per-operation cost and the account-rule scaling both have known fixes, and this is the baseline I'll measure them against. ## Where it stands The plugin works, has unit and functional tests (including one with a real fork), and the overhead numbers above come from running it against a syncing mainnet node. What it doesn't have yet is a way to catch a consumer up: if yours was down for an hour, you fetch that hour from the APIs yourself. That, and a few more attributes people ask for, is what I'd like to do next. The code is at https://github.com/serpent7776/hived-stinger, a fork of hive. The plugin isn't in a released hived yet, so trying it means building hived from that fork and adding `plugin = stinger` to the config. Hopefully you'll find this useful. Please let me know what you think, and if you have any suggestions or questions, just leave a comment.
Source: Introducing stinger: a hived plugin for matching operations of interest by @serpent7776

entry.content:
# Track Your Hive Witness in Home Assistant: Rank, Votes, Stake, Power Down & Portfolio Value ![Home Assistant Hive Stats Card](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/c0ff33a/23swgEFtNgPrGSMikMg5TuMEcwbT4fxDvmHD2EKW1mGeNtLnJpxUqpFEz9QsVuyX9qqti.png) ![Home Assistant Hive Stats Card lower portion](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/c0ff33a/23swg9rTWKojVs886y4QYFe9sGXFXBY8zdH1r5T7rNvacMPPNByev7CseJ3xtCFuBnDRV.png) If you run a Hive witness and already use **Home Assistant** at home, you can add a dashboard card that keeps an eye on your witness and your wallet. No custom integrations, no HACS, and no API keys. It uses Home Assistant's built-in REST and template features, Hive's public API nodes, and CoinGecko for prices. --- ## What the card shows **Witness** - Witness rank (active witnesses only, so disabled witnesses are skipped) - Total witness votes received (in MHP) - Missed blocks **Stake** - Your own Hive Power, and your effective HP after delegations - HP delegated out and delegated in - How many witness votes you've cast **Power down** - Whether a power down is running - Weekly payout and amount remaining - Countdown to the next payout **Wallet & portfolio** - Liquid and savings HIVE and HBD - Live HIVE and HBD prices - Total portfolio value (liquid HIVE + savings + own HP + HBD; HP delegated *to* you isn't counted) Prices are in **GBP (£)** by default. Changing currency is covered further down. --- ## How it works There are two parts: 1. **A sensor package (`hive.yaml`).** This calls the Hive API (`condenser_api.get_accounts`, `get_dynamic_global_properties`, `get_witness_by_account` and `get_witnesses_by_vote`) and CoinGecko, then turns VESTS into HP for you. 2. **A dashboard card.** A plain Lovelace card that displays those sensors. How often it updates: - Account data: every 5 minutes - Witness data: every 10 minutes - Rank: every 15 minutes - Prices: every 10 minutes - The VESTS → HP ratio: hourly --- ## Step 1: Edit the sensor package Copy the YAML below. Before saving it anywhere, **find and replace `YOUR_HIVE_ACCOUNT` with your account name**: lowercase, without the @. It appears **3 times**. ```yaml ############################################################################### # HIVE BLOCKCHAIN PACKAGE for Home Assistant # # >>> FIND & REPLACE every "YOUR_HIVE_ACCOUNT" with your account name # (lowercase, no @). It appears 3 times in this file. # >>> Fiat currency is GBP. To change, replace "gbp" (3 places) and "£". # # Install: save as /config/packages/hive.yaml and make sure # configuration.yaml contains: # # homeassistant: # packages: !include_dir_named packages # # Then restart Home Assistant (a YAML reload is not enough for new REST sensors). ############################################################################### rest: # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Account - resource: https://api.hive.blog method: POST headers: Content-Type: application/json payload: '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"condenser_api.get_accounts","params":[["YOUR_HIVE_ACCOUNT"]],"id":1}' scan_interval: 300 timeout: 20 sensor: - name: Hive Liquid HIVE unique_id: hive_liquid_hive unit_of_measurement: HIVE state_class: measurement value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].balance.split(' ')[0] | float(0) }}" - name: Hive Savings HIVE unique_id: hive_savings_hive unit_of_measurement: HIVE state_class: measurement value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].savings_balance.split(' ')[0] | float(0) }}" - name: Hive Liquid HBD unique_id: hive_liquid_hbd unit_of_measurement: HBD state_class: measurement value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].hbd_balance.split(' ')[0] | float(0) }}" - name: Hive Savings HBD unique_id: hive_savings_hbd unit_of_measurement: HBD state_class: measurement value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].savings_hbd_balance.split(' ')[0] | float(0) }}" - name: Hive Vests Own unique_id: hive_vests_own unit_of_measurement: VESTS value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].vesting_shares.split(' ')[0] | float(0) }}" - name: Hive Vests Delegated Out unique_id: hive_vests_delegated_out unit_of_measurement: VESTS value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].delegated_vesting_shares.split(' ')[0] | float(0) }}" - name: Hive Vests Received unique_id: hive_vests_received unit_of_measurement: VESTS value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].received_vesting_shares.split(' ')[0] | float(0) }}" - name: Hive Powerdown Rate Vests unique_id: hive_powerdown_rate_vests unit_of_measurement: VESTS value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].vesting_withdraw_rate.split(' ')[0] | float(0) }}" - name: Hive Powerdown Remaining Vests unique_id: hive_powerdown_remaining_vests unit_of_measurement: VESTS # to_withdraw / withdrawn are raw integers (VESTS x 1,000,000) value_template: > {% set a = value_json.result[0] %} {{ ((a.to_withdraw | int(0)) - (a.withdrawn | int(0))) / 1000000 }} - name: Hive Next Powerdown Raw unique_id: hive_next_powerdown_raw value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].next_vesting_withdrawal }}" - name: Hive Witness Votes Cast unique_id: hive_witness_votes_cast unit_of_measurement: votes value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].witness_votes | length }}" - name: Hive Witness Proxy unique_id: hive_witness_proxy value_template: "{{ value_json.result[0].proxy if value_json.result[0].proxy else 'none' }}" # ------------------------------------------------- Global props (VESTS -> HP) - resource: https://api.hive.blog method: POST headers: Content-Type: application/json payload: '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"condenser_api.get_dynamic_global_properties","params":[],"id":1}' scan_interval: 3600 timeout: 20 sensor: - name: Hive Per MVests unique_id: hive_per_mvests unit_of_measurement: HIVE value_template: > {% set fund = value_json.result.total_vesting_fund_hive.split(' ')[0] | float(0) %} {% set shares = value_json.result.total_vesting_shares.split(' ')[0] | float(1) %} {{ (fund / shares * 1000000) | round(6) }} # ------------------------------------------------------- Witness details - resource: https://api.hive.blog method: POST headers: Content-Type: application/json payload: '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"condenser_api.get_witness_by_account","params":["YOUR_HIVE_ACCOUNT"],"id":1}' scan_interval: 600 timeout: 20 sensor: - name: Hive Witness Votes Vests unique_id: hive_witness_votes_vests unit_of_measurement: VESTS # "votes" is raw VESTS x 1,000,000 value_template: "{{ (value_json.result.votes | int(0) / 1000000) if value_json.result else 0 }}" json_attributes_path: "$.result" json_attributes: - total_missed - last_confirmed_block_num - running_version - url - signing_key - name: Hive Witness Missed Blocks unique_id: hive_witness_missed_blocks unit_of_measurement: blocks value_template: "{{ value_json.result.total_missed if value_json.result else 0 }}" # ---------------------------------------- Witness rank (active witnesses only) - resource: https://api.hive.blog method: POST headers: Content-Type: application/json payload: '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"condenser_api.get_witnesses_by_vote","params":["",300],"id":1}' scan_interval: 900 timeout: 30 sensor: - name: Hive Witness Rank unique_id: hive_witness_rank # Disabled witnesses (null signing key) are skipped, so the rank matches # the "active" rank shown on most Hive witness pages. value_template: > {% set ns = namespace(i=0, rank=0) %} {% for w in value_json.result %} {% if w.signing_key != 'STM1111111111111111111111111111111114T1Anm' %} {% set ns.i = ns.i + 1 %} {% if w.owner == 'YOUR_HIVE_ACCOUNT' %}{% set ns.rank = ns.i %}{% endif %} {% endif %} {% endfor %} {{ ns.rank if ns.rank > 0 else '>' ~ ns.i }} # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Prices - resource: https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price?ids=hive,hive_dollar&vs_currencies=gbp scan_interval: 600 timeout: 20 sensor: - name: Hive Price unique_id: hive_price unit_of_measurement: "£" state_class: measurement value_template: "{{ value_json.hive.gbp | float(0) }}" - name: HBD Price unique_id: hbd_price unit_of_measurement: "£" state_class: measurement value_template: "{{ value_json.hive_dollar.gbp | float(0) }}" template: - sensor: - name: Hive Power Own unique_id: hive_power_own unit_of_measurement: HP state_class: measurement state: > {{ (states('sensor.hive_vests_own') | float(0) * states('sensor.hive_per_mvests') | float(0) / 1000000) | round(3) }} - name: Hive Power Effective unique_id: hive_power_effective unit_of_measurement: HP state_class: measurement state: > {% set v = states('sensor.hive_vests_own') | float(0) - states('sensor.hive_vests_delegated_out') | float(0) + states('sensor.hive_vests_received') | float(0) %} {{ (v * states('sensor.hive_per_mvests') | float(0) / 1000000) | round(3) }} - name: Hive Power Delegated Out unique_id: hive_power_delegated_out unit_of_measurement: HP state: > {{ (states('sensor.hive_vests_delegated_out') | float(0) * states('sensor.hive_per_mvests') | float(0) / 1000000) | round(3) }} - name: Hive Power Received unique_id: hive_power_received unit_of_measurement: HP state: > {{ (states('sensor.hive_vests_received') | float(0) * states('sensor.hive_per_mvests') | float(0) / 1000000) | round(3) }} - name: Hive Powerdown Weekly unique_id: hive_powerdown_weekly unit_of_measurement: HIVE state: > {{ (states('sensor.hive_powerdown_rate_vests') | float(0) * states('sensor.hive_per_mvests') | float(0) / 1000000) | round(3) }} - name: Hive Powerdown Remaining unique_id: hive_powerdown_remaining unit_of_measurement: HIVE state: > {{ (states('sensor.hive_powerdown_remaining_vests') | float(0) * states('sensor.hive_per_mvests') | float(0) / 1000000) | round(3) }} - name: Hive Powerdown Active unique_id: hive_powerdown_active state: "{{ 'Yes' if states('sensor.hive_powerdown_rate_vests') | float(0) > 0 else 'No' }}" icon: mdi:arrow-down-bold-circle-outline - name: Hive Next Powerdown unique_id: hive_next_powerdown device_class: timestamp availability: > {{ states('sensor.hive_next_powerdown_raw') not in ['unknown', 'unavailable', ''] and not states('sensor.hive_next_powerdown_raw').startswith('1969') }} state: "{{ states('sensor.hive_next_powerdown_raw') ~ '+00:00' }}" - name: Hive Witness Votes HP unique_id: hive_witness_votes_hp unit_of_measurement: HP state_class: measurement state: > {{ (states('sensor.hive_witness_votes_vests') | float(0) * states('sensor.hive_per_mvests') | float(0) / 1000000) | round(0) }} - name: Hive Witness Votes MHP unique_id: hive_witness_votes_mhp unit_of_measurement: MHP state: "{{ (states('sensor.hive_witness_votes_hp') | float(0) / 1000000) | round(2) }}" - name: Hive Portfolio Value unique_id: hive_portfolio_value unit_of_measurement: "£" device_class: monetary state: > {% set hive = states('sensor.hive_liquid_hive') | float(0) + states('sensor.hive_savings_hive') | float(0) + states('sensor.hive_power_own') | float(0) %} {% set hbd = states('sensor.hive_liquid_hbd') | float(0) + states('sensor.hive_savings_hbd') | float(0) %} {{ (hive * states('sensor.hive_price') | float(0) + hbd * states('sensor.hbd_price') | float(0)) | round(2) }} ``` --- ## Step 2: Add the package to Home Assistant How you do this depends on how Home Assistant is installed. If **Settings** has an **Add-ons** or **Apps** section, you're on **Home Assistant OS**: use Option A or B. If you see *"Apps require the Home Assistant Operating System"*, you're on **Docker/Container** or **Core**: use Option C. ### Option A: Home Assistant OS with the File editor app 1. Go to **Settings → Apps** (called **Add-ons** on older versions) and open the **store**. Search for **File editor**, then install and start it. Switch on **Show in sidebar**. 2. Open **File editor** from the sidebar. You'll be in the `/config` folder. 3. Click the **folder icon** (top left), then the **new folder icon**, and create a folder called `packages`. 4. Open `packages`, click the **new file icon** and name the file `hive.yaml`. 5. Paste in the YAML from Step 1, with your account name in it, and click **Save**. 6. Go back to `/config` and open `configuration.yaml` (see Step 3). ### Option B: Home Assistant OS with the Studio Code Server app If you'd rather use a VS Code-style editor: 1. Go to **Settings → Apps → store**, then install and start **Studio Code Server**. Switch on **Show in sidebar**. 2. Open it from the sidebar. In the file explorer, right-click the root of `/config` → **New Folder** → `packages`. 3. Right-click `packages` → **New File** → `hive.yaml`. Paste in the YAML and save (**Ctrl+S**). 4. Open `configuration.yaml` from the explorer (see Step 3). ### Option C: Docker / Container (or Core) by hand There are no apps on these installs, so you edit the files directly on the host. **1. Find your config folder.** It's the host folder mapped to `/config` in the container, the one containing `configuration.yaml`. In `docker-compose.yml` it's the line that looks like `- /some/path:/config`. If you're not sure, run this on the host: ``` docker inspect homeassistant --format '{{ range .Mounts }}{{ .Source }} -> {{ .Destination }}{{ println }}{{ end }}' ``` The path on the left of `-> /config` is your folder. Change `homeassistant` if your container has a different name. On a **Core** install the folder is usually `~/.homeassistant`. **2. Create the package file:** ``` cd /path/to/your/config mkdir -p packages nano packages/hive.yaml ``` Paste in the YAML. To save and exit, press **Ctrl+O**, **Enter**, then **Ctrl+X**. **3. Open `configuration.yaml`:** ``` nano configuration.yaml ``` Then follow Step 3 below. If your config folder is on a NAS or shared over the network, you can also do all of this in a normal desktop text editor. --- ## Step 3: Turn on packages in `configuration.yaml` Add these two lines to `configuration.yaml`: ```yaml homeassistant: packages: !include_dir_named packages ``` ⚠️ If there's **already** a `homeassistant:` line in the file, don't add a second one. Put the `packages:` line, indented, underneath the existing one. --- ## Step 4: Check and restart 1. Go to **Developer tools → YAML → Check configuration**. It should report the configuration as valid. 2. Do a **full restart**. A YAML reload won't load new REST sensors. - HA OS: **Settings → System → ⋮ (top right) → Restart Home Assistant** - Docker: `docker restart homeassistant` Give it a minute or two for the sensors to fill in. --- ## Step 5: Add the dashboard card 1. Open your dashboard and click the **pencil icon** (top right) to edit. 2. Click **+ Add card**, scroll to the bottom and pick **Manual**. 3. **Delete everything already in the box**, paste the YAML below, then click **Save**. ```yaml type: vertical-stack cards: - type: glance title: HIVE Witness columns: 3 entities: - entity: sensor.hive_witness_rank name: Rank icon: mdi:podium - entity: sensor.hive_witness_votes_mhp name: Votes icon: mdi:vote - entity: sensor.hive_witness_missed_blocks name: Missed icon: mdi:cube-off-outline - type: entities entities: - type: section label: Stake - entity: sensor.hive_power_own name: Hive Power (own) icon: mdi:lightning-bolt - entity: sensor.hive_power_effective name: Effective HP icon: mdi:lightning-bolt-circle - entity: sensor.hive_power_delegated_out name: Delegated out icon: mdi:arrow-right-bold - entity: sensor.hive_power_received name: Delegated in icon: mdi:arrow-left-bold - entity: sensor.hive_witness_votes_cast name: Witness votes cast icon: mdi:account-check - type: section label: Power Down - entity: sensor.hive_powerdown_active name: Powering down - entity: sensor.hive_powerdown_weekly name: Weekly payout icon: mdi:calendar-week - entity: sensor.hive_powerdown_remaining name: Remaining icon: mdi:progress-download - entity: sensor.hive_next_powerdown name: Next payout format: relative icon: mdi:clock-outline - type: section label: Wallet - entity: sensor.hive_liquid_hive name: HIVE (liquid) icon: mdi:wallet - entity: sensor.hive_savings_hive name: HIVE (savings) icon: mdi:piggy-bank - entity: sensor.hive_liquid_hbd name: HBD (liquid) icon: mdi:currency-usd - entity: sensor.hive_savings_hbd name: HBD (savings) icon: mdi:piggy-bank-outline - entity: sensor.hive_price name: HIVE price icon: mdi:chart-line - entity: sensor.hbd_price name: HBD price icon: mdi:chart-line-variant - type: entity entity: sensor.hive_portfolio_value name: Portfolio Value icon: mdi:cash-multiple ``` 💡 **Getting a configuration error?** The Manual card starts with some placeholder text, often including a `type:` line. If you paste underneath it instead of replacing it, you end up with two `type:` lines and Home Assistant rejects the card. Clear the box completely first. If you still get an error, removing the `type: vertical-stack` line also fixes it. --- ## Customising - **Currency:** in `hive.yaml`, replace `gbp` (3 places) with `usd`, `eur` and so on, and `£` with your symbol. - **API node:** the package uses `api.hive.blog`. If that's slow for you, replace each `resource: https://api.hive.blog` with another node, such as `https://api.deathwing.me` or `https://api.openhive.network`. Or run it against your own node, since you're a witness 😉 - **Rank:** this counts active witnesses only. If you're outside the top 300, it shows something like `>290`. - **Not a witness?** The card still works for any account. The witness rows just show 0. ## Troubleshooting - **Sensors show "unavailable":** check **Settings → System → Logs** for errors mentioning `rest` or `hive`. The usual cause is a typo in the account name, or `YOUR_HIVE_ACCOUNT` left in one of the 3 places. - **Entities not found on the card:** if you already had sensors with the same names, Home Assistant may have added `_2` to the new ones. Check **Settings → Devices & services → Entities**, search for "hive" and update the card to match. --- ## Ideas for next steps - Add a **history graph** of witness votes or HIVE price. - Create an **automation** to notify you when your rank changes or missed blocks go up. Questions and improvements are welcome in the comments 👇
Source: Home Assistant Users - View your Hive Witness stats at a glance with this dashboard card by @c0ff33a

entry.title: 3Speak: A Whole New Look, Built to Last

link.title: 3Speak: A Whole New Look, Built to Last

entry.content:
![3Speak dev update, November 4 to November 13, 2026](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSihc6YqpPY1CoyUWMcoduzRx9Rzzp3eHygUD1PWjPVSB/thumbnail.png) **The short version** - **3Speak 2.0 is live:** every page of [3speak.tv](https://3speak.tv) has a new design, on desktop and on phones, and the video editor got the same look. - **Home** gets a sliding Spotlight with short video previews, plus a side panel with the latest from the community and your groups. - **On phones,** the audio player docks above the bottom bar and follows your swipes: left and right to skip 15 seconds, up to open, down to close. - **Your wallet** claims rewards in one click and shows a QR code to receive HIVE and HBD. - **The Audio Editor is open to everyone:** cut, clean up and level your podcast, make audiograms that go out as Shorts, and record with a teleprompter. - **Invite people and earn:** 10% of what the people you invite earn from ads, for their first 3 months, paid on top by 3Speak. - **Playlists can hold whole podcast shows** from anywhere, and audio and playlists can be embedded on other websites. - Under the hood: smoother video playback, no ads paid out to crawlers, more than 5,000 new tests that found and fixed over 100 bugs, and new Snapie content filters. --- ## 🌐 3speak.tv website [new-3speak-tv](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv) · 18 merged changes, including the 2.0 release ([#566](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/566))
### 3Speak 2.0: a new look for every page Over the years, 3speak.tv grew one feature at a time. New things were built next to old code, each with its own look, and in some places it felt messy: buttons, menus and windows that didn't match from one page to the next. 3Speak 2.0 fixes that. Every screen, menu and window has been redesigned from one design system, so the whole site now has **consistent branding and modern, state-of-the-art design**: flat cards, the 3Speak red and blue, one set of icons and the same building blocks everywhere. We know most of us humans don't love change, especially on a site we use every day. But we think this one is super slick and awesome, and we hope that after a few days you will agree. We rely on your feedback. If anything broke, or something you used every day is now hard to find, tell us in the comments or with the **Feedback** button on the site, and we will fix it as fast as we can, as always. ![The 3Speak home page before and after 2.0](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRB5Kg4n8s3UGBJpxAWWbJAj6hg7nsRFkun9TWBr4MWnU/ba-home.png) - **Wider layouts:** on a big screen, Home now fits four videos side by side. - **A cleaner top bar:** Home, Shorts, Live, Audio and Groups always one click away, a Playlists menu with Watch Later and your history, and a **Create** button that sorts everything you can make into Video, Audio, Live and Others. - **The same look on every page:** watch pages, [Shorts](https://3speak.tv/shorts), the [Audio page](https://3speak.tv/audio), channels, communities, Settings, the uploaders and every popup. - **Faster first load:** icons, video players, popups and the emoji picker now load only when they are needed, and the Spotlight starts fetching its videos right away. The icon font alone went from 4.5 MB to 108 KB. On a prod-like build, the home page showed its main content in 1.25 s instead of 2.0 s on desktop, and in 5.2 s instead of 7.1 s on a phone on 4G. - **All 21 languages** are translated for every new and reworded text.
### On your phone
![3Speak on a phone before and after 2.0](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUi7Kj3rkukdWQegNk7WG8mJsk8FiLiB6NJ9G1qndEgic/ba-phone.png)
Every screen of 3Speak 2.0 was designed for phones too, not just squeezed down from the desktop. - **A bottom bar that stays put:** it is docked to the bottom edge of the screen and no longer jumps while you scroll, Firefox on Android included. On iPhones, the area of the home indicator is part of the bar. - **A big red + in the middle** opens everything you can create: a video, a Short, a story, audio or a playlist. - **Audio has its own tab** in the bar now, next to Home and Shorts. Groups moved into the account menu. - **The Spotlight comes first:** the featured video fills the top of Home with a big Play button, and Save and Share right next to it. - **The audio player docks right above the bottom bar,** so you can keep listening while you browse. - **Swipe the audio player:** swipe left or right to jump 15 seconds back or forward, swipe up to open the full player and down to close it. On the open player, a swipe down tucks it away again. - **The queue always shows what is playing.** Removing the playing track goes on with the next one, and an empty queue closes the player. - **One video per row,** with the title, the creator, the votes and the payout easy to read. - **Popups open from the bottom** as sheets, each with a title bar and a close button, so they are easy to reach with your thumb. - **Warm-up accounts** see their progress as a ring around their avatar in the bottom bar. - **Channel pages** keep Follow, Message, Tip and Share in one row, and on small screens Message shortens to "DM" so everything fits.
### Channel pages ![A channel page before and after 2.0](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPHnEggot3n7sZJ9Kw2u6tT3LBnXNeEWxoJk94Bi53Ceo/ba-profile.png) [Channel pages](https://3speak.tv/@badadib) got a calmer header: the name, a row of stats with the channel's linked profiles, and Follow, Message, Tip, Share and More as clear buttons. The tabs below hold Videos, Shorts, Audio, Playlists, Community, Supporters and Members, with a search for the channel next to them.
### A new Home ![The Home feed with the new side panel](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbDuhpED9ZQw8GfjqANoRf6zyBNdYMRz99EwhdRxRB1qd/home-feed.png) - **A sliding Spotlight:** the top of [Home](https://3speak.tv) moves through all featured videos, one every 7 seconds. On desktop it plays a short, muted preview of each one, and you can turn previews off under Settings, Appearance. - **A side panel next to your feed:** new audio, playlists and posts from the community, plus your groups. People still in their warm-up see their goals there. - **"Mark all as seen"** on the strip of new videos from people you follow: it comes back only when someone you follow posts again. - The feed tabs are now **Discover, Following, Interests and New**, and picking your interests in Settings uses the same picture tiles as the first-visit popup.
![The new welcome card for first-time visitors](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTHYKVVSbD3BNc7mxkjKBTkzo1qqZJkfd3WzXSVZqNdqZ/welcome.png)
First-time visitors are greeted by a **new welcome card**: five tiles that say what 3Speak is about (a real alternative to corporate social media since 2019, community-owned, creators earn from upvotes and ads, viewers and listeners earn too, and we never sell your data), with a big button to take the tour and one for the FAQ.
### Your wallet
![The new 3Speak wallet](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT8bWqWX8mnbvSRGmdX2ESSoFyWjvrXC4abBguG9b3xKM/wallet.png)
The [wallet](https://3speak.tv/wallet/badadib) is new too. When rewards are waiting, a banner shows how much, and **Claim** collects them in one click. **Receive** shows a QR code for your account, which can ask for an amount in HIVE or HBD and carry a memo. On phones, **Scan** in the Send window fills in the recipient from their QR code. A card shows your resource credits in plain words ("enough for about 458 posts right now"), and a chart shows what you earned in the last 30 days.
### The Audio Editor, for everyone
![The Audio Editor in the Create menu](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYH95iMrKY3rCrZufYZxrXZGkF8EhQRqWUmrfdSJYjoMu/create.png)
The **Audio Editor** is open to every creator, from the Create menu and from every track in the audio upload (**Edit audio**). It is made for podcasts, music and voice: - **Cut silences** finds the pauses and closes the gaps, and **levelling** brings your episode to podcast loudness. - Voice and music on their own tracks, fades, noise reduction, a music library and sound effects, for recordings up to 3 hours. - A **template** with your intro, outro and music bed, applied by itself to every new recording. - **Chapters** that end up in the MP3 and in the episode's description. - **Audiograms:** pick a piece of up to 2 minutes and design a vertical video with your cover, title and a moving waveform. Each one goes out as a [Short](https://3speak.tv/shorts) together with your audio, and on the Shorts page it opens the full episode.
![The teleprompter in the audio upload](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZCvP1R4TCebhDBMUpmiEp8V8GiEvsJo4g2MjXtZgcxn5/audio-upload.png)
The audio upload got better too: - A **teleprompter** for recording in the browser, in the upload and in the editor: write your script, and it scrolls at a steady speed or follows your voice. - **Make a transcript** writes down what you said (English for now) and puts it under your post text, ready to edit. - **Covers:** your playlist's cover is picked for you, and you can design your own cover with text and stickers. - The post description has the full editor, with emoji, GIFs, images and a preview. ([#555](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/555), [#556](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/556), [#557](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/557), [#559](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/559))
### Invite people, earn 10%
![Referrals in Settings](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdns6kTnPnWhpQr3Txi2FHqno19Nkn9gtvJsYEuuXjdt7/referrals.png)
Settings has your personal **invite link**. Invite someone with it, and you get **10% of their ad rewards** for their first 3 months, whether they earn as a creator, a viewer or a listener, plus **2% of their ad campaigns** if they advertise. 3Speak pays this on top: the people you invite keep everything they earn. Listening now earns from the same pool as watching, at the same rate. Switch on "Count my listening too" in the same tab. ([#546](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/546))
### Playlists and podcasts - **Whole shows in a playlist:** add any podcast from anywhere with the new **External shows** button, and its new episodes show up by themselves. - **Playlist types:** mark a playlist as Video or Audio, and audio playlists as Podcast, Music, Voice notes or Other sounds. Tracks uploaded into a Music or Podcast playlist take that type. - **Embed on your website:** every audio, audio playlist and outside podcast has an **Embed** button. A playlist embed always shows the latest tracks. - Audio cards show the **title of the post** instead of the recording's file name. ([#548](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/548), [#554](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/554))
### Small touches - **"Not interested" really works now:** videos you mark, and creators you hide with "Don't show this creator", stay out of every feed right away, also when you come back to a page later. ([#565](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/issues/565)) - **Powered by Hive:** a link to [hive.io](https://hive.io) in the account menu, on the About page and in the FAQ. ([#563](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/issues/563)) - **Hiding a creator hides everything they post:** videos, Shorts, audio, playlists and stories. - **Mark all read** really clears everything, stories and podcast episodes included, and is in the bell too. - **Escape closes windows**, and the top bar, notifications, comments and the upload picker work with a keyboard and screen readers. - **Scheduled posts** can be edited in a popup that matches the uploader. - Videos that **stall** on one server now load the next piece from another one within seconds. - Thumbnails hosted on Ecency load through our own image cache, so they show up for everyone. - Shorts and story captions no longer repeat the "Watch on 3Speak" footer. - Remix drafts opened later still post under the original. - Uploads show a short notice: copyrighted material declines its payout. - Accounts that can't upload now see why, with a way to reach us. ([#545](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/545), [#549](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/549), [#550](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/550), [#551](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/551), [#552](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/552), [#553](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/553), [#558](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/558), [#560](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/560), [#561](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/561), [#562](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/562)) --- ## ⚡ Feeds and API [3speakchecks](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks) · 27 changes The "checker" is the service behind 3Speak's feeds, ads, tips and the Audio page. ![Test coverage before and after](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUvtrs4fMoCoNhFhimEoUutUxRtNfG86Y8GNZ6nmtVA4W/tests.png) - **Tested like never before:** the checker went from 17% to 98.5% of its code covered by tests, on a throwaway database that can never touch real data or real money. Writing the tests found 70 bugs, and all of them are fixed, from a request that could crash the service to a few security issues. The video player (99.4%) and the website (1,417 to 4,251 unit tests) got the same treatment. ([#120](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/120), [#121](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/121), [#123](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/123), [#124](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/124), [#125](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/125), [#126](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/126), [#127](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/127)) - **No ads paid out to crawlers:** search engines and AI crawlers that render watch pages were "watching" ads, which took money away from creators with real viewers. In two days of logs, 38,578 of 69,652 ad requests came from them, and they are refused now. ([#141](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/141), [#142](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/142)) - **No ads on content that can't earn:** posts that decline their payout, and creators whose rewards are blocked, carry no ads at all. ([#143](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/143)) - **Audio ads, calmer:** at most one audio ad every 15 minutes per listener, and video tickers play in audio only when the advertiser chooses it. ([#116](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/116), [#117](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/117)) - **Referral bonus and listener rewards** behind the new Settings tab. ([#118](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/118), [#134](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/134)) - **A second checker in the US:** the site talks to whichever one answers faster for you, and every change now goes to the US one first. ([#132](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/132), [#133](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/133)) - **Thumbnails for videos that had none:** some apps upload without a thumbnail, which left 1,740 videos with the placeholder. They now get a frame from the video. ([#136](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/136)) - **Audio:** real post titles instead of file names, podcast hosts listed under Creators on the Podcasts tab, playlist types in feeds and RSS, and outside shows inside playlists. ([#128](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/128), [#130](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/130), [#131](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/131), [#141](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/141)) - **Faster, steadier:** a repeated search answers in about 2 ms instead of 2.5 seconds, and podcast crawlers can no longer slow down the whole site by reading every RSS feed at once. ([#127](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/127), [#135](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/135)) - Hidden creators and unlisted videos stay out of every feed, the search and its suggestions, and "Mark all as seen" support for the new-videos strip. ([#119](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/119), [#137](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/137), [#144](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/144)) --- ## 🎚️ Video editor [3speak-editor-suite](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite) · 11 changes - **The 3Speak 2.0 look:** the audio and Shorts editor now match the new site, with the same colours, icons, buttons and popups, and popups become bottom sheets on phones. ([#25](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/25)) - **Clearer camera errors:** the recorders used to say "Camera access denied" for every problem. Now they tell you what is really wrong, like a camera busy in a video call, and offer **Try again**. ([#25](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/25)) - **The audio mode** behind the Audio Editor, with MP3 export, templates, the audiogram studio and the teleprompter in the voice recorder. ([#15](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/15), [#21](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/21), [#24](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/24)) - **Flags:** press B to drop numbered, coloured markers on the timeline. They move along with your edits. ([#18](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/18)) - **Drafts remember the view:** the zoom and the selected clip come back when you open a draft. ([#18](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/18)) - **Taller or shorter tracks:** drag the handle under a track's name, and tracks scroll up and down when they don't fit. entry.title: Core dev meeting #85
entry.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Blvm5pvinHo Hello, here's the core dev meeting of the month. It's been a while, last time we all met in person at HiveFest so there's quite a bit to cover. AI generated summary, some mistakes may have slipped through so please listen to the meeting for the accurate info. # Me (@howo) - Gopherd: mostly unglamorous work now, optimizations, security fixes and getting the experience on par with hived. It's been producing quite a few blocks which is nice. - Floated the idea of a client identifier in the witness version field so voters can see which client a witness runs. Conclusion: since both clients have feature parity there's no real need yet, people can just say it in a post. We'll revisit later. - Two MRs that have been waiting for review for a while: - DHF `daily_pay` overflow: there's no upper bound, so a big enough proposal could overflow and crash the chain during maintenance. It would never get voted in, but no reason to leave it open. It's a hardfork change, so there's no rush. - Moderation audit log on hivemind: a new table logging every mod action (mute, unmute, pin, set role etc.) plus 3 endpoints (log, per account, moderator activity). No perf impact since mod actions are rare. - Side experiment I still want to get to: using hive + HAF as a data availability layer for the OP stack (Optimism) to get EVM compatibility as an L2, no L1 changes needed. # @blocktrades - Release is getting close. Dan estimates the pace is ~10x faster than at the start of the year thanks to AI. - Lite accounts are in testing, with the API up on api.syncad.com. Now is the time to send feedback (good-karma and asgarth are already looking at it). - REST API for hivemind is in. - HAF and all its apps now replay at the same time: a full node with every app (FYP and haf-stats included) replays in under 24h instead of ~2 days. - Big API speedups across HAF apps, especially hivemind and account history (no more timeouts on huge accounts). There's also an option to get discussions without vote data for lighter responses. - Denser: new chat, better proposals page, FYP page, doesn't load wax on every page anymore. The healthchecker component can now pick a different API node per API. - Beekeeper hardening following Gandalf's security feedback. - API node: tracked down slowdowns to a memory/garbage collection issue in drone (rust) and worked around it, and added load shedding against AI scraper bots. GitLab now requires login for non rate limited access. - AI went through all the open issues (43 of Gandalf's got closed in one night), labels were harmonized and old issues/MRs cleaned up. - Experimenting with speeding up hived replay/sync, not sure it'll make the release. # @mcfarhat - HAF FYP and haf-stats are now part of the HAF API node bundle. PeakD and Denser integrated FYP, Ecency is working on it. - FYP algorithm 1.4.1 is the default on a fresh deploy. Weights are configurable per node, the post window went to 48h so less active languages still get content, and storage went from 300GB to ~7.4GB. - haf-stats no longer locks hivemind and now records actual RC costs instead of estimates. - HiveSense: search by author and by time range is on the test API. - Block explorer: light vs full mode via an env var (hivescan.info and classic.hivescan.info), missed blocks and voting power on the witness list, top holders combine liquid + savings, phantom null/steem.dao balances fixed. - Actifit: big security hardening, Fitbit moved to Health Connect, signups in the mobile app. - HiveSense MR !148 has been waiting on CI for a while, Dan will follow up. Also welcome to @acid who joined for the first time!
Source: Core dev meeting #85 by @howo

entry.title: How to embed any Hive post on another website

link.title: How to embed any Hive post on another website

entry.content:
Mit der neuen Cyberspace-App könnt ihr jedes beliebige Hive Posting und auch Kommentare professionell in einer anderen Website einbinden. Das Feature funnktioniert so ähnlich wie auf X/Twitter. Um einen Hive-Artikel einzubinden, öffnet diesen auf [cyberspace77.com](https://cyberspace77.com/). Dann klickt auf die drei Punkte, wählt "Embed post" aus, und kopiert den Code auf eure Website. Voilà! Habe technisch mehrere Varianten getestet, dieses Feature zu implementieren. Anfangs nur mit einem iframe. Das Problem ist bei iframes allerdings, dass man die Größe im Nachhinein vom eingebundenen Frame aus nicht ändern kann, und das ist vor allem bei Posts von sozialen Medien ein Problem, da diese unterschiedlich lange sind und sogar im Nachhinein durch Edits die Größe verändern können. Daher benötigt man ein Hilfsskript, das die Postings in der richtigen Größe dynamisch einbindet. Theoretisch kann man das Posting auch ohne Skript einbinden, wenn man die richtige Größe des iframes statisch setzt, was allerdings aus obigen Gründen nicht empfehlenswert ist. Das Posting selbst ist aber wieder in einem iframe, in diesem Fall, was Vorteile in Bezug auf die Sicherheit hat. Nur ein kleines Open-Source-Skript muss dazu im Kontext der Website laufen, das man auch jederzeit nachprüfen kann. Habe mich designtechnisch im Moment gegen ein starkes Branding des Embed-Frames entschieden, damit man Hive-Artikeln auch professionell zum Beispiel auf News-Seiten einbinden kann. Ein zu starkes Branding oder ein zu auffälliger Krypto-Bezug könnte Newseditoren abschrecken. Der Inhalt und der Autor des Postings sollen im Vordergrund stehen. Was sagt ihr dazu? Habt ihr dieses Feature auf Hive auch vermisst? Wolltet ihr schon einmal ein Posting außerhalb von Hive irgendwo einbinden? ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSuoNex5rK9yL1G9oF57Dw39Wem556Dr43ptcRyZbf7e7/image.png) https://cyberspace77.com/ @cyberspace77 ## English With the new Cyberspace app, you can professionally embed any Hive post, including comments, into another website. The feature works similarly to how it does on X/Twitter. To embed a Hive article, open it on [cyberspace77.com](https://cyberspace77.com/). Then click the three dots, select “Embed post,” and copy the code to your website. Voilà! I’ve tested several technical approaches to implementing this feature. Initially, I used only an iframe. The problem with iframes, however, is that you can’t change the size of the embedded frame afterward, and this is especially an issue with social media posts, since they vary in length and can even change size later due to edits. Therefore, you need a helper script that dynamically embeds the posts at the correct size. Theoretically, you could embed the post without a script by statically setting the correct size of the iframe, but this isn’t recommended for the reasons mentioned above. The post itself, however, is embedded in an iframe, which offers security benefits. Only a small open-source script needs to run within the website’s context, and you can verify it at any time. From a design perspective, I’ve decided against heavy branding of the embed frame for now, so that Hive articles can be embedded professionally on news sites, for example. Branding that’s too strong or a crypto reference that’s too conspicuous could deter news editors. The content and the author of the post should take center stage. What do you think? Have you also missed this feature on Hive? Have you ever wanted to embed a post somewhere outside of Hive?
Source: How to embed any Hive post on another website by @vikisecrets

entry.title: I built a Hive witness widget for my desktop (dms/dux)

link.title: I built a Hive witness widget for my desktop (dms/dux)

entry.content:
I check the same three tabs most days: my witness rank, my wallet, and the price of HIVE. So I built the thing I wanted instead — a small DankMaterialShell (aka [dux](https://duxlabs.dev/)) plugin that puts it all on my bar and my desktop. It's called **HIVE Witness**, it's at [github.com/ausbitbank/hiveWitness](https://github.com/ausbitbank/hiveWitness), and today it's at **2.5.0** — the first public release. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ausbitbank/Eo1w14CtXDfwcJG8u9eyXdiwxdYTrBVs2cTTHAfQGVEB1kEinhWm2mmtYuVMzu5Qrto.png) ## What it does The bar pill is the glance: rank and votes by default, or rank plus portfolio value, or just one of them. Click it and you get the full card. The same card can sit on the desktop permanently, which is how I usually use it. The card shows: - **Witness standing** — rank, total votes, share of the vesting pool, and missed blocks. - **Balances and stake** — liquid HIVE and HBD, savings, staked HP, and delegation. - **Powerdown** — the next weekly drip, a countdown to it, and how many cycles are left. - **Portfolio value** — in USD, AUD, NZD, CAD, GBP or EUR, priced from CoinGecko with the node's HBD ticker as a fallback. - **A 7-day sparkline** — hover for values, with a 7d change pill. If the account isn't a witness, it still shows balances and stake, and the witness-only rows read `—` instead of making something up. ## Installing it You'll need DankMaterialShell `>= 1.2.0` and `curl` on your `PATH`. Any supported compositor should be fine. ```bash git clone https://github.com/ausbitbank/hiveWitness.git \ ~/.config/dms/plugins/hiveWitness ``` Then tell DMS to rescan: ```bash dms ipc call plugin-scan reload hiveWitness ``` If it was already enabled and the new code doesn't show up, restart the shell: ```bash systemctl --user restart dms.service ``` Enable **HIVE Witness** in Settings → Plugins, then set your account in the plugin settings. A fresh install says **No account set** — I deliberately left the default empty rather than shipping someone else's account. ## A note on privacy It only talks to public endpoints: your configured Hive node, CoinGecko for price, and Frankfurter (with an open.er-api fallback) for FX. There's no telemetry and no analytics. The only account it asks about is the one you give it, and only public on-chain data comes back. The optional CoinGecko key is the one caveat. DMS stores it in plain text in `~/.config/dms/plugin_settings.json`, and it's visible to local processes in the `curl` argument list while a request runs. Leave it blank unless you need the higher rate limit — the keyless endpoint is rate limited, but it works. HTTP goes through `curl` because that's the supported DMS process interface. Requests are launched with an argument array rather than a shell, so settings can't inject commands. ## What I'd like from you First up, this is a pretty niche thing, I honestly don't know if any other hive witnesses are using dms/dux but it exists so I may as well release it publicly anyway. This is the first public release, so I'd genuinely like to hear where it's wrong or where it's missing something. If you run a witness, the useful feedback is usually "this number doesn't match what the explorer says" — that's a bug, and I want it. If you don't run one, tell me whether the card is still useful for stake and portfolio, because that was a deliberate design choice. Issues and PRs are open. There's a [`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`](https://github.com/ausbitbank/hiveWitness/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) with the architecture notes and the QML traps I hit, in case you want to poke at it. ```bash git clone https://github.com/ausbitbank/hiveWitness.git \ ~/.config/dms/plugins/hiveWitness dms ipc call plugin-scan reload hiveWitness ``` MIT licensed. *My usual apologies for being crap at blogging and going silent for so long. I'm still around, just getting my ass kicked by life in general and struggling to find motivation to post publicly. <3
Source: I built a Hive witness widget for my desktop (dms/dux) by @ausbitbank

entry.title: 3Speak: Lightning Strikes, Podcasts Play, Thumbnails Shine

link.title: 3Speak: Lightning Strikes, Podcasts Play, Thumbnails Shine

entry.content:
![3Speak dev update, October 28 to November 4, 2026](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXwcohU9s42mDcdy6LmmNeUxsb3unP8YtSqMWvAtXHVJz/thumbnail.png) **The short version** - **Tip with Lightning:** any Lightning wallet can tip a creator, no Hive account needed, and creators can get tips in their own wallet. - **Import your videos** from YouTube or TikTok, with title, description, tags and thumbnail filled in for you. - A **thumbnail editor** in the uploader: text, stickers and any frame of your video. - **The Hive galaxy:** a 3D map of a channel's follows, to discover new creators. - **Stories** are open to every Hive account. - **3Speak is a podcast app now:** follow any podcast in the world, with charts, chapters, transcripts, offline listening and a full podcast player, plus sponsor spots and a pop-out player for 3Speak audio. - Under the hood: a rebuilt encoder for community operators, smarter retries for uploads, Butter Drive for big files and a new Snapie release. --- ## 🌐 3speak.tv website [new-3speak-tv](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv) · 10 releases, all live
### Tip with Lightning Every tip window now has a **Lightning** tab. Anyone with a Lightning wallet can tip a creator, no Hive account needed: the tip goes through the creator's v4v.app address, and a paid invoice is picked up by itself. ![The Lightning tab in the 3Speak tip window](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRN2AuiK2X3FAakMQH92bF8xLRo1a6z1xr8fmRjVH4PEy/tip.png) - Creators can also receive Lightning tips **in their own wallet** (Settings, Connections tab). - You can tip **without signing in**, and set up **monthly tips**. - Lightning tips show under [Supporters](https://3speak.tv/@badadib?tab=supporters), in sats. - Tip buttons on [Shorts](https://3speak.tv/shorts), in the audio player, and now also in the 3Speak video player and the audio embed on other sites. ([#536](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/536), [#540](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/540))
### Import your videos Bring your videos over from YouTube or TikTok. First, prove the channel is yours: 1. Open **Settings** (the gear at the top), go to **Connections** and then **Linked profiles**. 2. Pick the platform and copy your personal 3Speak code into your channel's public description. 3. Enter your channel and press **Verify**. Once it is linked, you can remove the code from your description again. ![Link your channel in Settings, then import](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUqNG3R6AqV63eFTaR5xQKL3fBnyWiQvoaD6LTHUWVVAm/link.png) Then use **Import videos** on your profile or in the upload window, or open [Import videos](https://3speak.tv/youtube-import). Title, description, tags and thumbnail are filled in for you, and you can import a whole batch at once. ([#536](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/536), [#537](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/537), [#544](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/544))
### A thumbnail editor in the uploader Step 2 of the [upload](https://3speak.tv/upload) now has a thumbnail editor. Pick any moment of your video, zoom and drag the frame, add text in 26 fonts with an outline or a box behind it, and place stickers, including 3Speak and Hive branding or your own images. **Download** saves exactly the picture that gets uploaded. On phones and tablets our server cuts the frame for you, so it works there too. ([#544](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/544))
### The Hive galaxy
![The Hive galaxy on 3Speak](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVwb5jAZUwaHPTg6zSk6vnxoAP8pbkBmGdF59gmfsXWSA/galaxy.png)
On desktop, the planet button on a profile opens the **Hive galaxy**: a 3D map of who a channel follows and the creators those follows lead to. Look at a channel's Following, its Followers or the friends who follow each other, and choose how deep to scan, from an Orbit of 120 accounts up to Deep space with 5,000. Accounts that the same people follow form **circles**, so you can see the little communities around a channel at a glance. Next to the map, **Creators to discover** lists the accounts many of the scanned people follow, and filters keep it to active accounts, a minimum reputation or creators with videos on 3Speak. Drag to turn the map, scroll to zoom, click a star to focus it and click the centre to fly back. Try [badadib's galaxy](https://3speak.tv/galaxy/badadib). ([#539](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/539), [3speakchecks #101](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/101))
### Stories for every Hive account Any logged-in Hive account can now post a 24-hour [Story](https://3speak.tv/shorts), from the Upload menu or from your own avatar in the stories row. Hovering an avatar in the row turns it around to a creator card: when they last posted, their bio and their follower, video, short and audio counts. ([#535](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/535), [#542](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/542))
### Podcasts and the new Audio page The biggest change of the week: the [Audio page](https://3speak.tv/audio) is now a full podcast app, for 3Speak audio and for any podcast out there. ![Add any podcast to 3Speak](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbHi7CUb2z6cpzNnz8YuQCrSD1tueoAx8EZHLY2cUExFG/add-podcast.png) - **Any podcast, not just Hive:** follow a show under External by searching for it, pasting its RSS feed, an Apple Podcasts or Overcast link or the show's website, or importing an OPML file from another app. - **Find new shows:** top charts for your country and category, trending podcasts by language, and a People search that finds the shows a host or guest appears in. - **Show and episode pages** with seasons, trailers, chapters marked on the timeline, transcripts that follow along, and the hosts and guests. - **Mine, Discover and Trends** split the Audio page into three views, and phones get a Player tab of their own. ![The 3Speak audio player, button by button](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZgfnuBDaMFFGUPp6x3qRsYXmVwyryzRwzigJsAkEBCPa/player-buttons.png) - **A real podcast player:** speed from 0.5x to 2x, 15-second skips, a sleep timer, Voice boost and Skip silence, casting to a speaker or TV, and your phone's lock screen controls. - **Share a moment:** a link that starts at the current time, or a clip of 15 to 90 seconds. - **Listen offline:** save episodes and 3Speak audio, and without a connection the Audio page opens your downloads. - **Never miss an episode:** new-episode alerts in the bell and as push notifications, and shows can add new episodes to your queue by themselves. - **Tip podcasters** in sats, straight from the podcast's own payment details. - **Every 3Speak audio has its own page**, and an all-audio playlist can be followed like a podcast. The full tour, with a screenshot for every button, is in [our podcast post](https://peakd.com/@mantequilla-soft/3speak-the-whole-podcast-universe-now-on-hive-2026-10-31). ([#536](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/536), [#539](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/539))
### Added since the podcast post ![Audio spots on the 3Speak advertise page](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNh8EsKt6eLaK4C2SdcwEZUxAjTgMdpCLfqJmn3pvWZtM/audio-ads.png) - **Sponsor spots in audio:** advertisers can book spoken tickers or their own audio clip on the [advertise page](https://3speak.tv/advertise). Creators choose in Settings whether ads play on their audio. - **A pop-out player** on desktop that fits whatever window you give it. - **A smarter queue:** tapping a cover while something plays adds it to the queue, and playlists offer **Add all** or **Add new**. - **Comment, Hype and reblog** any 3Speak audio right from the player. - **Continue listening** on [Mine](https://3speak.tv/audio?view=mine), and what you listened to shows in your Watched history, in a new Audio tab. - **New audio in [Discover](https://3speak.tv/discover):** the last 3 days of audio, one per creator. - **Earn while you listen:** agree once in Settings and your listening counts toward listener rewards, which start once we have checked the numbers. - 3Speak shows you follow under External get votes, comments, Hype and tips, and warm-up musicians and podcasters can now upload audio too. ([#538](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/538), [#539](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/539), [#540](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/540), [#541](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/541), [#543](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/543), [#544](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/544))
### Small touches ![Emoji in comments and menus that open on hover](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTvPf5DreWJrTYXjwRuedRRfDu6LDi87iwXyRqsSMPb7t/touches.png) - Type `:` in any comment box for an emoji list, and `:fire:` turns into 🔥. - The bell, Share, chat, settings and profile menus open when you rest the mouse on them. - Video previews on cards fade in and out smoothly. - Sharing a vertical video from your phone to 3Speak opens the Shorts uploader. - Profiles keep their Hive badges when a Hive server is busy: the site switches servers by itself. - "Mark all read" now clears the newest notification too. - The tip nudge no longer stops autoplay and channel surfing.
